findings.element: Status filter - reachable only via the "Add filter" menu in the filter bar
findings.finding: The only control that can filter to a specific status is hidden inside the Add filter menu, while the always-visible tab row offers just five coarse groups.

findings.element: Segmented status tab row + Status filter chip (two controls, one dimension)
findings.finding: Two independent controls filter status with no visible precedence, and the documented mitigation (a contradicting tab reads 0) only hides the empty result - it never tells the user the Status chip is what emptied the tab.

findings.element: "All" segmented tab (label reads 31)
findings.finding: The All tab promises 31 transactions but the list renders 25, and every other tab's count matches its rows exactly - so 6 transactions are counted but not reachable.

findings.element: Date range, Platform, Add filter and Status chips in the filter bar
findings.finding: Clicking a filter chip a second time does not close its panel, so the chip reads as a toggle but does not behave as one.

findings.element: Row ⋯ menu items — 'Sync now', 'Rollback sync', 'Archive'
findings.finding: Three of the four items in the per-row ⋯ menu carry no click handler at all, so choosing them does nothing and the menu gives no response.

findings.element: 'Actions' column link on every row (label is 'Sync', 'Retry' or 'View sync' depending on status)
findings.finding: The row action link is labelled with an imperative verb but always navigates to the transaction detail page instead of performing the action, while the identical verbs in the bulk bar act on the spot.

findings.element: Bulk action bar — '⟳ Sync now' button (#head-bulk, index.html:2298)
findings.finding: Sync now is the only bulk action that fires with no confirmation step; Rollback, Cancel, Archive and Unarchive all confirm first.

findings.element: Bulk confirm dialogs + 'Select all N' scope link (#scope-msg → selectAllTotal, index.html:2313-2315)
findings.finding: Destructive bulk confirms identify the selection only by count, and 'Select all' extends it to rows the user has never seen because only 25 of the 31 filtered rows are rendered.

findings.element: Transaction info cell (.txn-cell) on rows with no customer
findings.finding: When a transaction has no customer name the cell falls back to nothing and renders only the raw gateway id, with no placeholder explaining why.

findings.element: table header row / 'Select all on page' checkbox (bulk action bar)
findings.finding: Unchecking 'Select all on page' does not restore the table header row that the bulk bar replaced, so the user is left with a table that has no column headers and no header checkbox.

findings.element: Page header button 'Import historical data'
findings.finding: 'Import historical data' is styled as a live primary header action but clicking it produces no dialog, no navigation and no feedback of any kind.

findings.element: Bulk action bar — 'Cancel' and '×', plus 'Archive' and 'Unarchive' side by side
findings.finding: The bulk bar presents seven equal-weight controls including two that read as dismiss ('Cancel' and '×') and two that are mutually exclusive for any one selection ('Archive' and 'Unarchive'), with nothing indicating which applies to the rows selected.

findings.element: Bulk action bar — Archive confirm dialog / 'Unarchive' action
findings.finding: The Archive confirmation promises the rows 'can be restored later', but the documented status surface (6 segmented tabs and 19 statuses in 5 groups) contains no archived scope, so there is no recorded way to list archived rows and select them for 'Unarchive'.

findings.element: Bulk action bar 'N selected' count + the Archive/Rollback/Cancel confirm dialogs, after a status tab or filter chip changes
findings.finding: Switching a status tab while a selection is live silently re-scopes what the bulk actions will operate on without resetting the bar that reports the selection — the exact FLT-2 shape, moved from filters to selection.

findings.element: Bulk-bar master checkbox (chk-all-bulk) after the 'Select all 31' scope escalation
findings.finding: Unchecking select-all leaves 6 invisible transactions selected while every checkbox on screen reads unchecked, and the bulk bar stays armed over that invisible selection.

findings.element: Empty state ('No transactions in the last 90 days' + 'View all time' primary button) when the Status chip and the status tab contradict
findings.finding: The screen's only zero-row explanation names the one filter that is not responsible whenever the two status controls contradict each other, and its primary remedy cannot resolve it.

findings.element: Bulk 'Sync now' dialog ('Syncing N transactions…') and the bulk success alerts ('N transactions archived.' / 'rolled back.' / 'cancelled.')
findings.finding: Bulk actions announce an in-progress or completed state that nothing else on the screen reflects, and the design defines no path for the operation failing or half-succeeding.

findings.element: Status group "Successful" — segmented tab "Successful" and the "Successful" group header in the Status filter panel, which list "Skipped" and "Excluded from sync" alongside "Synced"
findings.finding: "Skipped" and "Excluded from sync" are transactions that were never posted to the books, yet both are grouped under "Successful", so the tab count presents unposted transactions as completed.

findings.element: Dashboard "Needs attention" card, "?" tooltip above the "50 transactions ›" link that navigates into the filtered list
findings.finding: The tooltip defines the group as failures only, but "Needs attention" also contains "Synced with warnings" and "Deleted with warnings" — transactions that did reach the books.

findings.element: Bulk bar "↩ Rollback" confirmation dialog; same banned terms in the "Sync status" column tooltip, the dashboard Sync card tooltip, and the dashboard Accounting card tooltip
findings.finding: The prototype uses "accounting platform" and "accounting system" — both explicitly disallowed — instead of "accounting company" for the software or "books" for the ledger, including in the one dialog that warns about deleting posted entries.

findings.element: Bulk action bar → "↩ Rollback" confirmation dialog
findings.finding: The Rollback confirmation is the only destructive action on the page that tells me something "will be deleted" without also telling me it can be undone, while the neighbouring Archive and Cancel dialogs both reassure me explicitly.

findings.element: Table → "Sync status" badge "Not parsed" on row po_1TKnR6E4pygkgelb8eE1Ff03, under the "Needs attention" tab
findings.finding: "Not parsed" is a software word, not a business word, and nothing on the screen explains it — the only tooltip on the page is on the column header and just says the status describes my accounting system.

findings.element: Status segment tab "Successful" → rows badged "Excluded from sync" and "Skipped"
findings.finding: The "Successful" tab lists transactions whose own status says they were never synced, so the tab label and the row contradict each other on the one question I actually care about.

findings.element: Row actions — the "Sync" / "Retry" / "View sync" link in the Actions column, and every item in the row ⋯ menu
findings.finding: The per-row primary action is an <a> with an onclick and no href, and all ⋯ menu items are plain <div class="dd-item"> — none of them has an href, tabindex or role, so none is in the tab order or operable by keyboard.

findings.element: Selection controls — 25 .row-chk row checkboxes, #chk-all, #chk-all-bulk, and the "Select all 31" scope link in the bulk bar
findings.finding: None of the 27 selection checkboxes has a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby, and the scope escalation to all 31 rows is an <a onclick> with no href, tabindex or role.

findings.element: Bulk action bar replacing the table header row (#head-bulk / #head-normal)
findings.finding: Selecting a row sets #head-normal to display:none, which removes every <th> column name from the table, and the swap is announced by nothing — there is no aria-live region and no focus move.

findings.element: Segmented status tabs (All / Needs attention / Ready to sync / In progress / Successful / Deleted)
findings.finding: The tabs are real buttons but expose their selected state only through a CSS class — there is no role="tab"/aria-selected, no aria-pressed and no aria-current anywhere in the file, and the .partial state (segment contains the active status but is narrower than it) has no ARIA equivalent at all.

note: Round 1 verified PASS 2026-08-26. 27 findings across 7 lenses, variant 1 only. Variant 2 / V7 side sheet and the transaction detail page are unreviewed.
